summary:
I built an interactive planner for the Moon south pole challenge. You compare candidate landing sites and dates by sunlight and Earth contact, and a sky view shows where the Sun and Earth sit on the horizon.

It has a site comparison table with sunlit %, Earth-in-view % and longest dark spell, a polar map, a 360° sky view with a time scrubber and play button, an elevation timeline, and a site-by-day heatmap. You can add your own coordinates, change the date window, and raise a terrain horizon to see how crater walls cut power and communication.

I checked the ephemeris against the lunar phases for this month. The Sun and Earth positions come out right, though I haven’t opened the page in a browser, so the layout and charts are unchecked. The site coordinates are approximate and the Moon is modeled as smooth, so use it for comparing sites and dates rather than mission design.
